finalists.title: Install a four-pin UV lamp and capture its free end in the Flex robot’s retaining clip
finalists.classification_meaning: Original robot-equipping operation and essential contact topology are verified; a small CPU mechanism/clearance study is justified using explicitly approximate dimensions. This is not a YAM clearance certificate, native demonstration, source-perfect CAD claim, or acceptance prediction.

importance.real_person: Technician assembling or maintaining the Opentrons Flex laboratory automation robot’s purpose-built HEPA/UV enclosure accessory.
importance.real_work: Install manufacturer-supplied18W2G11 bulbs in the robot enclosure module; these provide controlled enclosure decontamination as part of the actual automated pipetting workcell.
importance.source_chain: Manufacturer Flex hardware/manual describes the robot, purpose-built roof module, supplied bulbs and installation step7; UV specification names exact lamp-base standard. No generic room lamp is relabelled as a robot component.
importance.occupation_count: Not required for direct robot equipping category; no laboratory-worker or janitor total is borrowed.
importance.strongest_objection: UV enclosure equipment might be interpreted as general lab infrastructure rather than direct robot equipping.
importance.response: The documented module mounts onto the actual Flex robot, uses attachment/door interlocks and is sold/instructed as its dedicated enclosure; installation is literal physical equipment of the robot. This resolves the generic-lab-infrastructure objection at the specified task scope.

real_procedure.exact_steps: After the module is attached, unbox supplied bulbs; each has4prongs that fit a recessed underside power receptacle. Push prongs into receptacle, then gently press the free end until retaining clips snap around it. Manufacturer installation.md step7.
real_procedure.source_read: Original Markdown and the corresponding installation figure were read/viewed. uv-specs.md and product-specs.md also read.

verified_hardware_inventory.component: One supplied18W actinic compact fluorescent UV-C bulb
verified_hardware_inventory.known: Single-cap2G11 base,4pins;18W,0.375A,58V nominal; twin long glass tubes on an insulating base in maker installation figure.
verified_hardware_inventory.material: Glass light-emitting tubes; metal pins; insulating base material not published.
verified_hardware_inventory.size: Exact bulb dimensions/mass not published in the inspected robot manual. For bounded CPU screening only, parameterize roughly200–250mm total length,35–45mm width,15–25mm depth and50–150g. These ranges are engineering estimates, not manufacturer specifications.
verified_hardware_inventory.starting_state: Unwrapped spare bulb in ordinary protective cradle, base exposed for acquisition.

verified_hardware_inventory.known: Recessed receptacle on module underside receives all4bulb pins by axial push. No screw/bayonet turn is specified.
verified_hardware_inventory.unknown: Pin pitch/diameter, keyed base shape, engagement depth and contact/friction forces are not dimensioned. Use a compatible actual2G11 standard pattern and explicitly estimate dimensions for CPU screening; dimension it before native hardware reproduction.
verified_hardware_inventory.essential: All4physical pin/channel alignments and base shoulder seating must remain explicit; no proximity attach or invisible socket weld.

verified_hardware_inventory.known: Separate clip supports the free glass end after plug insertion; original image and text explicitly show a snap-capture action.
verified_hardware_inventory.unknown: Exact clip dimensions, material and force curve not specified. Topology is documented; spring compliance can be parameterized.
verified_hardware_inventory.essential: Clip lips must physically open/displace and close past bulb section, providing retention after release; a scripted latch triggered by nearness erases the skill.

verified_hardware_inventory.known: 87×64×14cm,~20kg. Robot frame is sheet metal/aluminum. Module remains fixed throughout task, so YAM does not lift20kg.
verified_hardware_inventory.support: Full-size roof module or original full-size lamp bay supported at a documented service height in its original downward-facing orientation; an ordinary rigid service stand may react insertion forces. Retain all surrounding geometry that can block the hands.
verified_hardware_inventory.approximation: Other lamp bay, filters, fan internals and wiring may be omitted only where they do not affect the manipulation corridor. Do not shrink lamp, socket or remote support span.

verified_hardware_inventory.known: No handheld installation tool is specified.
verified_hardware_inventory.proposal: Ruler/feeler gauge, photographs, low-voltage continuity tester and a light spring-scale retention check after robot releases. Functional UV illumination is outside this physical installation task; module remains unpowered.

finalists.initial_configuration: A fixed, unpowered, cool module lamp bay has its original recessed2G11socket and remote retainingclip empty. One correct supplied lamp lies in a protective cradle within reach, with its plastic base exposed. Other lamp is already installed and is an obstacle only if source geometry places it in the approach. Whole module remains supported; no fictitious enlarged grip tabs or reduced-scale roof.
finalists.instruction: Fit the supplied lamp into the module’s four-pin socket, press its free end securely into the retaining clip, and let go with both hands.
finalists.central_physical_ability: Register an extended fragile part into a multipin socket and complete a second, separated compliant capture without pulling or levering its seated terminal end out. This is coupled two-interface assembly, not screwing a bulb into one socket.
finalists.bimanual_or_horizon: One normal hand grasps/stabilizes the insulating base and guides axial pin entry. The other supports the long twin-tube section as its free end is brought to the remote clip, controlling pitch and bending load. The exact handoff/press sequence is to be established by CPU study; bimanual necessity is not claimed as proven. A single-arm success remains valid if physically possible.

physical_scoring.partial: 0.25: all4pins are physically engaged in their actual channels and base shoulder is seated to proposed≤1mm gap, but free end is not captured.0.5: base is seated and clip lips have physically closed past the glass section, but the robot is touching either interface or they have not settled.0.75: both interfaces retained and hands clear, but independent completion test has not passed.
physical_scoring.full: 1.0: base shoulder seated, all4pins engaged, glass end retained by original clip, hands at least30mm clear for2s; assembly remains in original support geometry after a gentle independent proposed1N withdrawal/downward test. On real hardware, continuity across both lamp-electrode circuits verifies actual4pin socket contact without powering the UV ballast. No electronic hidden success flag is needed.
physical_scoring.measurement: Front/side photos with ruler show base shoulder gap and glass behind clip lips; feeler gauge verifies≤1mm gap; light spring scale tests retention; optional low-voltage ohmmeter checks the two filament contact circuits. Pin depth/gaps/force margins above are benchmark proposals, not OEM tolerances.
physical_scoring.invalid: Broken/cracked glass, visibly bent pins, broken clip/socket, bulb not matching2G11standard, or movement/damage of original support that changes the task. Simulation may treat glass as rigid and separately track visible excessive deformation/contact hazards; do not claim calibrated fracture physics.
physical_scoring.reset: Gently release actual remote clip, withdraw base axially, inspect pins/glass/clip, and return the same unpowered lamp to its protective cradle. No intended consumable, though damaged lamps or fatigued clips must be replaced.

YAM_screen.object_scale_mass: Single estimated50–150g/200–250mmlamp is within likely payload range; exact mass not verified. No need to handle fixed20kgmodule.
YAM_screen.normal_grasps: Plastic base estimated35–45mm cross-section is below nominal94mmaperture; real pad contact width, exposed base length and stable support on glass must be tested, not inferred from aperture alone. Normal second hand may support tube pair gently instead of pinching individual pins.
YAM_screen.palm_wrist: Recessed socket and roof lip may block palm/wrist even with reachable pins. Preserve module lip and other bulb in source-correct positions; screen full315collisionhulls perarm, not tip reach.
YAM_screen.tools: No installation tool or tool-wrench requirement. Test gauges are external scoring instruments, not robot substitutions.
YAM_screen.fixture_reaction: Original module casing/socket mount and service stand react axial insertion and clip snap. Fixture must not artificially guide bulb or open the clip for it.
YAM_screen.critical_path: Acquire base, carry long body clear, align4pins, enter axially, support free end during clip press, release bothhands, retract. Exact small angular motion follows actual compatible socket/clip geometry; do not invent a large hinging motion that would bend seated pins.
YAM_screen.verified_status: PLANNING PLAUSIBILITY ONLY; noYAMIK/collision/grasp-force/path execution or full-score demo ran.

faithful_fidelity_plan.core: Rigid longglassbody with actual base/pins;4socket channels and shoulder; spring-contact/friction retention at socket; remote actual clip represented with explicit compliant lips and physical contact. Both interfaces remain mechanically meaningful afterrelease.
faithful_fidelity_plan.allowed_approximation: Noncritical housing details and ballast internals omitted; dimensions within declared source-unpublished ranges used for bounded screening; clip flex can be rigid spring-loaded jaws matching actual snapcapture rather than continuum elasticity. Glass can be rigid with fracture omitted if explicitly disclosed.
faithful_fidelity_plan.forbidden: Invisible weld after bulb enters a radius; base rotates to lock despite source axialpush; giant dummygrip; shortened span; holdingclip artificially open; count alone from object proximity.
